about.heading: A student building real experience
paragraphs: I'm a Computer Science student with a strong interest in software development and computer science fundamentals. For roughly the last two years I've been exploring programming through personal projects, tutorials, and academic work — not professional employment, but deliberate practice.

I enjoy building small applications end-to-end: designing the layout, writing the code, hitting bugs, reading error messages, and fixing things. I care about understanding and debugging code rather than just generating it, and I'm especially interested in how AI can assist — and where it can't replace — careful software engineering.
My goal is to grow into a well-rounded software developer through internships, more ambitious projects, and continuous learning. I'm currently working towards that, one project at a time.

projects.title: Product Studio
projects.problem: Design assignments often stop at static Figma wireframes. The assignment required designing an animal-care MVP, an AI education landing page, and an AI content workflow, but I wanted to prove I could actually build the final, interactive product instead of just drawing it.
projects.contribution: Built the entire 5-page interactive site from scratch using pure HTML, CSS, and Vanilla JavaScript. Designed three distinct visual identities (Emerald for Practo, Violet for Education, Coral for Carousel) unified by a shared design system. Wrote a custom JavaScript engine to handle 3D card tilting, mouse-tracking spotlight glows, and magnetic button physics. Built a settings drawer that uses localStorage to persist theme, density, and motion preferences. Built dynamic rendering using HTML <template> tags for provider cards, programme cards, and carousel slides.
projects.learned: How to engineer CSS 3D transforms and JavaScript pointer events to create tactile, premium micro-interactions. I also learned how to build a robust design system using CSS custom properties, manage state across multiple pages via local storage, and ship a fully responsive, accessible frontend without relying on external frameworks.

projects.title: THE EXEMPTION
projects.problem: A college event project exploring public data, hidden trackers, data aggregation, location tracking, behavioural analysis, and digital privacy.
projects.contribution: Built an interactive data-broker competition concept using web technologies — HTML, CSS, and JavaScript on the front end, with Node.js/serverless functionality and Supabase for the backend.
projects.learned: How interactive data experiences are structured, how serverless and Supabase fit together, and how to design around a privacy-focused brief.

projects.title: This Portfolio
projects.problem: Needed a clean, honest way to present my skills and projects to internships and recruiters.
projects.contribution: Built from scratch — HTML, CSS, and JavaScript on the front end, with a small Python static site generator that renders pages from JSON data.
projects.learned: How static site generation works, how to keep content in one place, and how to design a responsive multi-page site without a framework.

projects.title: OmniShare — Secure Share Portal
projects.problem: Three common sharing tasks (QR codes, shortened URLs, secure file/text sharing) each require separate tools, most of which want an account. Built one app that does all three without registration.
projects.contribution: Built end-to-end: Flask backend with QR generation (qrcode + Pillow), URL shortener with click tracking and 96-hour expiry, secure share with password protection and automatic cleanup, plus an HTMX + Tailwind frontend. Deployed with Gunicorn.
projects.learned: How to structure a multi-feature Flask app, manage in-memory vs. on-disk state, run background cleanup with threading, use HTMX for partial-page updates, and ship a Python web app to production.

projects.title: LeaveMail — Smart Leave Assistant
projects.problem: Parents often struggle to write formal leave emails — mobile typing is slow, formatting is unclear, and email clients are complex. Existing tools assume desktop use and English fluency.
projects.contribution: Built a mobile-first Flask app with four email templates, six visual themes, Web Speech API voice input, quick presets, and a full accessibility layer (high contrast, large text, reduced motion). Includes settings, local history, and PIN/password/pattern lock with server-side hashing.
projects.learned: How to design for accessibility-first use, handle session-cookie limits safely, hash credentials before storage, escape user input to prevent XSS in previews, and ship a Flask app on Render.

section_templates.achievement_detail:
Achievement Case Study

From Data Fragments to Digital Portraits

The Exemption: A Digital Privacy Awareness Programme

The Exemption was a digital privacy awareness programme presented by the BVM Holy Cross College Computer Science Department and ASSET. My session introduced the hidden journey of personal data: everyday details such as location, device information, browsing activity, and interests can be gathered from different sources and assembled into a profile.

The programme explored how real-time advertising auctions and data brokers can turn those fragments into predictions and targeted ads. To make the topic hands-on, I built a team-based browser game. Teams examined a target profile, selected the relevant data packets from a larger set, and tried to reconstruct the profile.

The activity turned an abstract privacy issue into a practical challenge: each data point may seem ordinary on its own, but combining them can reveal much more about a person. The programme also included discussion of data aggregation, location tracking, behavioural analysis, and the advertising ecosystem.

I presented the session as part of the programme on 23 October 2026. The poster describes the goal as giving participants practical exposure to real-time bidding and data-broker mechanics; the programme chart lists my session as “Class by Edwin Tony.”

Certification & Case Study

UI/UX Design Programme

Completed with Sapphire IQ

I recently completed a two-month UI/UX Design programme offered by Sapphire IQ. This certification provided me with a structured introduction to user experience and interface design, complementing my Computer Science studies.

Throughout the programme, I explored core design principles, including UX research, usability, navigation, information architecture, and design thinking. Applying these concepts practically, I worked on a comprehensive UX case study for the Gurully Test Preparation App. This involved analysing user needs, structuring the app's flow, and thinking through interface decisions from a user-centric perspective.

As a Computer Science student interested in software development, understanding the design pipeline is invaluable. This experience has improved my ability to empathise with end-users and consider usability alongside functionality when building web and software applications.
